Shelley Moore Capito

REP candidate for U.S. Senator, West Virginia · Incumbent

U.S. Senator from West Virginia (incumbent)

Shelley Moore Capito is the Republican incumbent U.S. senator from West Virginia and is running for a third six-year term. She was first elected to the U.S. House in 2001 (term began that year) and chairs the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee. She won the May 12, 2026 Republican primary over state Sen. Tom Willis and faces Democrat Rachel Fetty Anderson and Constitution Party candidate S. Marshall Wilson on November 3.

Where Capito stands

Energy prices and permitting reform
Says producing more domestic energy and building infrastructure to deliver it will lower energy bills. Is pushing a permitting reform bill that she says cuts time and expense without giving up environmental review.
Iran
Says she is encouraging the president to bring the Iran situation to a close, and links that to lowering prices at the pump.
Taxes
Supported the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which created tax breaks on tips and overtime.
SNAP / food assistance
Says SNAP grew during COVID and that changes aim to eliminate fraud and abuse and return the program to its pre-COVID size.
College athletics
Co-sponsored the Protect College Sports Act, which sets national name, image and likeness and transfer rules for college athletes. Says it prevents exploitation of student athletes and puts education first.
Infrastructure
Names finishing Corridor H, improvements to U.S. Route 35, and other road projects as priorities she wants to keep working on.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, West Virginia (2001–2015)
  • U.S. Senator, West Virginia (2015–present)
  • Chair, Senate Environment and Public Works Committee
  • Member, Senate Appropriations Committee; chairs the Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education subcommittee
  • Fourth-ranking member of Senate Republican leadership
  • Endorsed for re-election by President Donald Trump
